title: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It’s not so easy.
gist: The FDA has proposed withdrawing Amgen's Tavneos, a drug for ANCA-associated vasculitis approved in 2021 on a narrow advisory vote. It alleges that ChemoCentryx unblinded and cherry-picked patients for re-adjudication to flip a failed pivotal trial, and it cites liver injury and eight deaths. NEJM has retracted the trial paper and the EU and UK have pulled the drug. Amgen insists the drug works, and the law's stepwise hearing process means US withdrawal could drag on.
